description: Trading (selling a looted item, prices, the Realm Exchange) and crafting (combines, materials, skill gains).

lines.text: Anyone in need of {item}? Make me a fair offer.
Check the Realm Exchange first so you know what {item} usually fetches.
A merchant's price is the floor. Anything above that is a good deal.
Another batch of combines done. Skill went up by one, so I call it a win.
Spent my last silver on materials again. Crafting is a hungry trade.
Keep at it. The first hundred points are the slowest.
Selling {item}. Fair offers welcome, no lowballing please.
Got {item} off my last kill. Any use to anyone before I vendor it?
What is {item} worth these days? I honestly have no idea.
Does anybody know if {item} is worth keeping, or is it merchant fodder?
My pack is stuffed with {item} and I am too stubborn to vendor it.
Hauled {item} all the way back to town. It had better be worth something.
Putting {item} on the Realm Exchange. Let us see if anyone bites.
Is it just me, or has the Realm Exchange gone quiet lately?
Listed three things on the Exchange and sold none. My prices must be too proud.
The merchant offered me next to nothing for {item}. Insulting, really.
Weighing up whether to vendor {item} or keep it for a twink.
Buying spare drops, anyone? I need coin for a new set of armor.
Who knows a good price for {item}? I would rather not get fleeced.
Sold everything to the merchant and still cannot afford that new shield.
Every time I sell something cheap, someone tells me it was worth triple.
Haggling is not my strong suit. I fold at the first counteroffer.
Bags full again. Time to visit the merchant and pretend I am rich.
Looking to swap {item} for something a {class} can actually use.
Does {item} have any real use, or is it just pretty?
WTS {item}. Make an offer.
WTB a decent shield. Not fussy about looks.
Coin purse is looking thin. Selling off the odds and ends.
Merchants never haggle. That is what makes them so maddening.
Picked up {item} out in {zone}. Someone tell me it is rare.
My pack smells of wet fur and old bones. Selling the lot.
Never sure if a drop is worth the wait on the Exchange or just a quick sale to the merchant.
Spent an age sorting loot. Half of it is junk and the other half is a mystery.
I kept {item} for weeks thinking it was valuable. It was not.
Anyone else hoard drops and then forget why they kept them?
Finally cleared the junk out of my vault. Felt like spring cleaning.
Selling to a merchant is quick. Selling to people is an adventure.
Would anyone part with some coin for {item}? It is in good shape.
Gems from {zone} sell nicely, if you can find a buyer.
Thinking of keeping {item} as a trophy. The thing nearly killed me.
Please tell me {item} is not vendor trash.
Need coin for a horse ride and a repair bill. Selling my spares.
Repair bills are eating me alive. Every coin counts right now.
Got a few spares on me, if anyone nearby wants a look.
Lucky drop today. Not saying what it is until it sells.
Loot from Darkness Falls always seems to find a buyer.
Magical drops sell far better than the plain ones. Learned that the slow way.
Does any crafter here buy raw materials? I have a pile of them.
Bartering for {item}. Open to swaps, not just coin.
Selling the gear I outgrew. Ideal for anyone a few levels behind me.
If {item} does not sell soon, it goes to the merchant. Last chance.
Exchange or merchant? I ask myself that every trip to town.
Drops from the Shrouded Isles fetch a nice price back home.
Price check on {item}, anyone?
Do any of you collect odd drops? I have a few strange ones.
Three trips to the merchant and my pack is still half full.
Selling loot is the one fight I always lose.
Guild, before I vendor {item}, does anyone want it?
Guild, anyone need cheap gear for an alt? Clearing out my vault.
Trading talk in town is louder than any battle I have seen.
Somebody just paid good coin for my junk. I feel almost guilty.
The merchants in Camelot could talk a giant out of its club.
I do my selling in Ludlow. Smaller crowds, same coin.
Took my drops to Cotswold. The merchant there looked at me with pity.
Jordheim traders bargain like they are fighting a war.
Mularn merchants will buy anything. I tested that theory thoroughly.
Haggling with a dwarf in Jordheim is a sport of its own.
Selling in Tir na Nog today. Those crowds will take anything shiny.
The merchants in Mag Mell drive a harder bargain than any monster.
Sold my spare loot in Ardee. Pockets jingle again.
Depends who is buying. Ask around before you settle.
See what the Exchange lists it for, then go a little under.
If nobody bites on the Exchange, the merchant is always there.
Vendor it. Not worth the hassle.
Hold on to it. Somebody always needs that sort of thing eventually.
Never take the first offer. People expect a little haggling.
Price it to sell, not to sit.
Magical items are worth asking about. Plain ones, just vendor them.
If it has decent bonuses, someone outfitting a twink will want it.
Ask a crafter. They know what materials are worth better than anyone.
Merchants pay the same every time. People pay what they feel like.
Selling cheap beats carrying it around for a week.
Do not undercut too hard. You only teach people to wait.
Wait for a busier hour. More buyers about.
Patience. Good items sell, they just take their time.
Nobody pays top coin for something every hunter has a stack of.
Sounds like merchant fodder to me, sorry.
That kind sells steady. Do not let it go too cheap.
Honestly, the merchant is fine for that one.
Split the difference and call it fair.
Try a swap instead. Coin is not the only currency.
Someone in {guild} was hunting for one of those. Ask around.
Ask the guild first. Friends pay fair.
Put it up on the Exchange and forget about it. It sells or it does not.
Lower it a touch and it will move.
Keep it if your class can use it. Coin comes back, good gear does not.
No point shopping around merchants. They all pay the same.
Sell the junk, keep anything with stats. That is my rule.
I would make an offer, but my purse is empty too.
Not much call for those lately, from what I have seen.
Ha, I sold one of those for a song once. Learn from my mistake.
People will pay more, but merchants never argue.
Light and valuable, keep it. Heavy and cheap, vendor it.
Check what others are asking, then do not be the greedy one.
Never trust a price you hear in chat. Check for yourself.
Be firm. A fair price is a fair price.
Whatever you do, ask around before selling it to a merchant.
The Realm Exchange is the safest bet for that.
Haggle a bit. It is half the fun.
Too many folks selling those right now. Hold off a while.
Weapon drops sell faster than armor, in my experience.
Ask yourself if you will miss it. If not, sell.
Rule of thumb: if a merchant will buy it, someone else might pay more.
Start high. You can always come down, never up.
Weaponcrafting all evening. My arms ache more than after a fight.
Another failed combine. Lost half the materials too.
Skill went up twice in a row. The forge loves me today.
Bought a stack of metal bars and they vanished in an hour.
Armorcrafting is a lesson in patience. And in poverty.
Tailoring cloth caps until my eyes cross.
Fletching arrows by the hundred. My fingers are full of splinters.
Alchemy is the only trade where failure smells this bad.
Spellcrafting is half sums, half praying nothing explodes.
Overcharged a piece and it blew up in my face. Never again. Well, maybe again.
Made my first masterpiece! Suddenly the whole trade feels worth it.
Ninety-four percent quality again. So close and yet so far.
Grey recipes teach nothing. Time to move up a tier.
Which trade should I pick up? I keep changing my mind.
Thinking of taking up spellcrafting. Is it as costly as everyone says?
Guild, I am at the forge tonight. Anything you need made at my skill?
Made a set of armor for a guildmate. Proud of how it turned out.
How are the {guild} crafters getting on with their skills?
Leatherworking is holding back my armorcraft. Grinding it up now.
Metalworking is the bottleneck. It is always the metalworking.
Woodworking is dull, but my bows will not make themselves.
Gemcutting takes longer than the spellcraft itself.
Herbalism up a point. Alchemy, here I come.
Siegecraft is not glamorous, but somebody has to build the rams.
My time at the anvil is the only quiet time I get.
Spent all my loot money on materials. Again.
Hammering away while everyone else hunts. Someone has to make the gear.
Failed three combines in a row. The forge hates me.
Recipes keep getting harder and the bars keep getting pricier.
Each new tier of metal is a fresh drain on my purse.
Made a pile of weapons nobody wants. The merchant takes them at a loss.
Crafting is cheaper than buying, they said. They lied.
Mixed a batch of potions. Smells awful, works wonders.
Brewing poisons for the stealthers in the guild. Mind the fumes.
Fletching arrows for the archers of {guild}. Nobody else will.
A ninety-nine percent piece feels different in the hand. Quality matters.
First time at the forge. How do people do this all day?
Gained a skill point on my very last combine. Perfect timing.
The crafting trainer says I have potential. I think he says that to everyone.
Every crafter I know is broke. Now I understand why.
Armor I made is walking around the realm on other people. Strange feeling.
Taking a break from hunting to raise my tailoring.
My guild needs a weaponcrafter. Guess who volunteered.
Cloth is cheap, but the hours spent tailoring are not.
Just one more combine. I have said that forty times now.
Spellcraft gems are tiny, expensive and very easy to waste.
Put an alchemy charge on my own weapon. Feels good to make my own.
Materials stocked. Time for a long night at the anvil.
The secondary skills always lag behind. It is maddening.
One more skill tier, then I am going hunting. I promise.
Nothing beats the sound of a successful combine.
Too many swords, not enough hands. My crafting overflow needs a home.
Bowyers get no respect until the archers run dry.
Picked a tradeskill at last. Wish me luck and deep pockets.
The forges in Camelot are always crowded. I wait my turn and grumble.
Albion armor takes a steady hand. Chain links do not forgive mistakes.
Jordheim smiths taught me everything. Mostly how to fail gracefully.
Nothing warms the bones like a Jordheim forge on a cold day.
Crafting in Tir na Nog. The hall is full of tailors tonight.
Hibernian armor is lovely to craft. Every piece looks like a carving.
Check your secondary skills. They hold you back more than you think.
Make whatever costs least to make. Skill is skill.
Stay on the harder recipes. That is where the gains come from.
Sell the results to the merchant. You get a bit of the cost back.
Failures happen. The lost materials sting less over time.
Spellcraft is costly, but people always need it done.
Pick the trade your guild is missing. You will never lack customers.
Armorcraft pays well once you are high enough.
Weaponcraft is popular. Tailoring has less competition.
Alchemy pays, if you can stand the smell.
Fletching is cheap to raise, from what I hear.
Grats on the skill-up!
A masterpiece? Well done, that is the dream.
Never overcharge more than you can afford to lose.
I gave up crafting long ago. Respect to anyone who sticks with it.
Buy materials in bulk. Saves running back and forth.
Stick with it. The high-end pieces are worth the grind.
Good on you for crafting for the guild.
Bring a full purse. You will need it.
I feel that. My purse has been empty for weeks.
Patience. The forge rewards the stubborn.
Take a break, go hunt, come back with coin.
Ask the guild crafters for tips. Most of them love to talk shop.
That is how it goes. Some days the forge just says no.
Watch the quality on your work. Higher quality sells better.
Same here. My materials vanish faster than my patience.
